pages.text: The pages keep to old houses: $(li)land-shaping$(li)biomes and their rulers$(li)time and weather$(li)suns, moons, and stars$(li)sky anomalies$(li)creature laws$(li)landmarks$(li)colors and the things they stain$(li)stranger marks such as $(thing)Random$(), $(thing)Age Effect$(), and $(thing)Low Gravity$().

$(thing)Color pages$() speak in pairs. First the hue, then the vessel. $(c)Blue$() before $(c)Water$() stains the waters blue. The same order binds sky, fog, grass, foliage, clouds, and other willing things.

$(thing)Biome pages$() may name one country, a favored list, or a pattern by which many countries take turns. The calmest Ages I have walked were often the plainest: one biome, clearly chosen, with no argument left for the ink.

$(thing)Low Gravity$() stands alone. It loosens the world's grip on your bones, softening falls and making every leap suspiciously heroic. The Age notices such tampering, though it complains less than it does for a true Age Effect.
